clue.text: Late caller gets double

parts.note: late can mean deceased, as in 'the late king'
someone who rings a doorbell or telephone is a ringer

explanation.surface: A late-night caller turns out to be somebody's double.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' reads as a time of day but means no longer living.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is a person who looks exactly like another, a double or lookalike.

clue.text: Skilful lower socio-economic groups supported by newspaper

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece supported by another sits on top of it

parts.note: in British social grading, D and E are the two lowest socio-economic groups
FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A newspaper is praised for its skill in serving poorer readers.
explanation.walkthrough: UK market research grades households A, B, C1, C2, D and E; 'supported by' puts DE above FT in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft is a synonym for skilful, meaning neat and nimble in handling things.

clue.text: A drill set up since regularly requiring oxygen

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: to drill a hole is to bore it

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word since, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: An exercise drill has been organised since it improves oxygen intake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns BORE into EROB; 'regularly' takes IC from sInCe.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobic describes organisms or exercise that depend on a supply of oxygen.

clue.text: Criminal can reorder key handbook for working out values

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook can rearrange the key in a reference book of calculations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' is the anagram signal; 'reorder' looks like one but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A ready reckoner is a book or table of precomputed figures for quick calculation.

clue.text: Propose master should have name for daughter

indicators.note: for says the second letter goes in place of the first, swapping the D for N

parts.note: to master something is to dominate it

explanation.surface: A father suggests a son should take a name in place of the daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' replaces the D at the start of DOMINATE with N.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to put them forward or propose them for a role.

clue.text: Break out in laughter up there

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the words laughter up there

explanation.surface: Laughter breaks out somewhere upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across laughtER UP There.
explanation.definitionFit: To erupt is to burst forth suddenly, as a volcano or a crowd does.

clue.text: Record of police department sent back to arrest son

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold or catch, so one piece holds the other inside it
sent back means the letters run in reverse

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A police department's file is returned after a son's arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns CID into DIC; 'to arrest' places S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, the vinyl kind played on a turntable.

clue.text: Time of endless dry wit — a good experience at first

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: irony is a dry form of wit

indicators.note: at first takes just the opening letter of experience

explanation.surface: A period when deadpan humour was a fine new experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts IRONY to IRON; 'at first' gives E from experience.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Age is a prehistoric period, the era when iron tools came into use.

clue.text: Instrument of fraud sure to see American sent down?

parts.note: a con is a swindle or fraud

indicators.note: in a down entry, sent down shifts the letter lower, one place later in the word

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fraudster's tool will get an American sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent down' moves the A in CERTAIN one place later, giving CERTINA; 'sent down' also suggests jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A concertina is a small bellows-driven musical instrument with buttons at each end.

clue.text: Part of body needing listener to be in shape

indicators.note: to be in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: form is a synonym for shape
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Getting in shape needs a part of the body that can listen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be in' is the containment signal: the listener goes inside the shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The forearm is the section of the arm between elbow and wrist.

clue.text: College study incorporating Republican symbol on coat of arms

parts.note: uni is informal for university, a college

indicators.note: incorporating means taking something into the body of the word

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn

explanation.surface: A college study of a Republican heraldic emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporating' puts R inside CON to make CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is a heraldic beast, famously a supporter on the UK royal coat of arms.

clue.text: 1 Across may be otherwise wanted in italics as absent

indicators.note: otherwise suggests the letters are arranged differently
absent says the letters of the word as are taken away from the pool

parts.note: taken as written, to be removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: Words wanted in italics are missing from the text.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and S from WANTEDINITALICS and rearrange the remaining thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A double who looks exactly like someone could be a sibling born from the same egg.

clue.text: Developing polythene bead is unacceptable

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters are changing into something new

explanation.surface: A plastic bead that keeps developing is not acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond the pale is an idiom for conduct outside the bounds of decency.

clue.text: Receiver's glass collection

definitions.note: read as Receiver is: the apostrophe s is the link word joining definition to wordplay

parts.note: crystal is fine glass
a set is a collection of things

explanation.surface: Someone's collection of fine glassware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver's' looks possessive, but it means 'Receiver is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crystal set is an early simple radio receiver using a crystal detector.

clue.text: Sports ground charge to include European copy

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground

indicators.note: to include means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A sports ground fee is raised to include copying a European model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' places E inside RATE to give REATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recreate something is to make it again, reproducing or copying it.

clue.text: Leaders of any truly international show

indicators.note: leaders are the front runners, so the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: The heads of any truly international exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders of' gives A and T; 'show' is a verb, meaning demonstrate.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness to or demonstrate that something is true.

clue.text: Bird from Brazil perhaps needing opening

parts.note: a Brazil is a kind of nut, given here by example
a hatch is an opening such as a trapdoor

explanation.surface: A bird from Brazil needs a gap to get out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazil' looks like the country but is the nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small songbird that climbs tree trunks and cracks nuts.

clue.text: Follows lecture in case of sepsis

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the case of a word is its outer letters, here the first and last

parts.note: a talk is a lecture

explanation.surface: A medical lecture follows a case of blood infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' means the outer letters of sepsis; 'in' says the lecture sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To stalk someone is to pursue or follow them stealthily.

clue.text: State requiring a student with a couple of degrees

parts.note: L for learner, from the plate on a learner driver's car
BA and MA are two university degrees, Bachelor and Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A US state requires each student to hold two degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the states of the USA, in the Deep South.

clue.text: Purpose of oil used by female

parts.note: unction is anointing with oil, or the ointment itself

explanation.surface: A woman asks what the oil she uses is for.
explanation.definitionFit: A function is the purpose or role something serves.

clue.text: Going to the heart patients here?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, patients are ... in a hospital

explanation.surface: Hospital patients, perhaps cardiac ones, heading somewhere?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into IN WARDS, where hospital patients are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Inwards means towards the inside or centre of something.

clue.text: Illegal profit, in a way, before distribution of wealth

indicators.note: before puts the first part ahead of the second
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
a gain is a profit

indicators.note: distribution suggests the letters are spread around in new order

explanation.surface: Making money in some fashion before sharing out the riches is illicit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the profit going inside 'a way'; 'distribution of' signals the riches being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something against the law is forbidden by statute, so illegal.

clue.text: African expression of disapproval — second one

parts.note: tut is a click of the tongue showing disapproval
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An African tuts disapprovingly, then a second does too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are an ethnic group of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Trained gymnast must keep tense

indicators.note: must keep says the words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: A well-trained gymnast must stay taut.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across trainED GYmnast.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means nervous or on edge, tense with anxiety.

clue.text: Mist may be a worry on the borders of Shropshire

indicators.note: in an across entry, on puts a piece after the one it sits on
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to fret is to worry

explanation.surface: Fog could be a concern near the edges of Shropshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders of' gives SE; Shropshire is an English county on the Welsh border, far from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fret is a coastal fog that rolls in from the sea, a mist.

clue.text: Bride's intention about religious education loomed large

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a bride intends to wed
RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: A bride's plans for a religious wedding hang over everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts RE inside TO WED.
explanation.definitionFit: Towered means rose high above, looming over everything around.

clue.text: Gin most of Labour perhaps rejected

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters read in reverse
most of drops the final letter

parts.note: Labour is a British political party, given by example

explanation.surface: Gin is mostly turned down by Labour politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts PARTY to PART; 'rejected' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for catching animals, a sense of trap.

clue.text: Cheating — could be attractive keeping notes exchanged

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.note: dishy is informal for good-looking

indicators.note: exchanged means the letters swap places

explanation.surface: Swapping notes with a good-looking classmate counts as cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged' rearranges the notes; 'keeping' says the attractive word holds them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonesty covers cheating, lying and fraud: lack of integrity.
